lines: A rocky outcrop rises above the ravine. The wind is fierce here — you're exposed, higher than the surrounding terrain.
An old metal post stands at the center, instruments still attached beneath decades of dust and dark-adapted moss. Survey Marker Delta-7.
From this vantage point, you can see further into the Nightside than ever before.
You brush the moss from the instruments and extract the data core. Old geological readings, thermal maps, subsurface scans — decades of automated measurements, patiently recording.
Archivist Solen will be fascinated by this.
Beyond the ravine, the darkness stretches endlessly. But it's not empty.
In the far distance, you can see faint lights — not Lighthouses. Something else. Tiny pinpricks of bioluminescence scattered across the vast dark.
Unbounded settlements. People living out there, in the permanent night, by the glow of cultivated fungi and geothermal vents.
Something that was always there. The world is bigger than you thought.
